text:
sara: Heads up — multiple customers reporting 503s on hosted inference around 09:12 UTC. High rate of timeouts and gateway 5xxs.

devon: Looking at the gateway logs now. Upstream responses show repeated 502/503 from infer-runner pool-7.

mike: Correlated node events show GPU OOMs and container restarts on g-node-a12. Lots of restart loops.

anita: Logs include a segfault in the attention kernel right before OOM. Paste sample:
```
[2024-11-12T09:12:35Z] infer-runner[pid=2345]: cudaErrorOutOfMemory: out of memory
[2024-11-12T09:12:35Z] infer-runner[pid=2345]: attention_kernel.cu:245: segfault (invalid device pointer)
[2024-11-12T09:12:36Z] containerd: killing container infer-runner due to exit code 139
```

ira: Which customers impacted? Need to notify support/CS.

sara: Two enterprise tenants so far — acme-ai and fineprint. CS already notified acme; they're seeing timeouts and retry storms.

devon: Repro steps that trigger it: high concurrency plus long context. Example curl to reproduce (internal loadgen):
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"g-qat-8k","input":"<4k tokens>...","batch_size":20,"max_tokens":1024}'
```
High concurrency (20+) + seq_len ~4k seems to push memory and hit the crash.

support_bot: Alert: automatic fallback routing engaged for acme-ai (policy=latency_first) — routed to smaller-model variant to reduce failures.

mike: Temporary mitigation in progress: reducing max_batch_size on pool-7 from 16->4 and enabling stricter prefetch caps. Rolling patch to the daemonset now.

anita: Observed stack shows an invalid pointer before OOM — could be stale KV cache pointer combined with aggressive prefetch + container restart. Not a plain OOM.

devon: I can reproduce locally with the synthetic harness using sequence length + concurrency. Building an instrumented runner (ASAN) to capture repro traces. Trace ID: trace-987.

ira: Ops: can we throttle these tenants' concurrency limits and apply routing to dedicated fallback pools until we have a fix?

mike: Throttling applied via rate-limiter policy for acme-ai and fineprint. Also enabled routing to smaller non-quantized variant. Monitoring metrics.

deploy-bot: deploy #infra/limit-batch -> success on pool-7 (2 pods restarted)

sara: Customer update sent: told acme about temporary throttling + fallback routing. CS escalated; they asked for ETA and postmortem.

devon: Proposed next steps:
- instrument KV cache lifecycle and add guardrails for cache invalidation
- add prefetch memory accounting to reject batch if estimated memory > threshold
- reproduce with ASAN and escalate to kernel vendors if segfault persists

anita: Opening ticket with attention-kernel maintainers, attaching trace-987 and core dump. ETA 24h for initial triage.

ira: Uploaded heap/profile dumps to the incident page and linked to this thread. Ping @sara for any customer escalations.

sara: Thanks all. I'll keep CS updated and own the postmortem. Monitoring for 2 hours; if stable we'll close. :white_check_mark:
